title: Sanctions Screening

origin.publisher: Lursoft IT (report); listing data from the US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list
origin.title: Viktor Anatolijevitch BOUT - Sanctions record (SDN entry 8279)
origin.clearance_note: A sanctions-record report generated by Lursoft's public sanctions search for OFAC SDN entry 8279, Viktor Bout, a convicted arms dealer on the US sanctions list. Downloaded manually, because the site answers scripted requests with a Cloudflare challenge. Every listed value (names, aliases, birth data, programme, remark) is public US government data, also published by OFAC at https://sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov/Details.aspx?id=8279, and several sanctions-screening vendors use this same listing as their example report. The listing is kept unredacted at the document owner's decision. The one replacement is the requester's IP address, which Lursoft prints in the page header of each generated report: it identifies whoever downloaded the file, not the listed subject, and was replaced with 198.51.100.245 from the RFC 5737 documentation range, using document-types/scripts/redact.py, which removes the underlying text rather than covering it. The PDF metadata was cleared. Verified: the original IP is not extractable from the committed PDF and appears nowhere in this collection folder.

redactions.note: The original value is deliberately NOT recorded here. The rules file used by redact.py stays outside the repo.

replaced.what: requester's IP address in the report header

notes: The request asked for page 1 and named no fields. These tell one story, the listing a screening hit returns: who, on which list, under which programme, since when, and why. The subject's name is featured: a sanctions screen is a name match, so this document type cannot be shown without one, and the subject is a publicly sanctioned individual whose listing is US government data. subject_name occurrence 1 is the report heading; occurrence 0 is the Full name row of the Names table. The remark ends mid-name ('Compagnie Aerienne des Grands') because Lursoft's report truncates it; extraction returns it as printed. Extraction varied between runs on the same parse. One run returned null for the alias Vitali SERGITOV's quality, 'Strong', which is printed alone at the top of page 2, split from the rest of that alias's rows by the page break (the parse keeps it, as 'Quality: Strong' after the page break). Another grounded the remark to its 'Remark' label rather than to the text. The committed extraction has both right. The page 2 dates read OFF in inspect_fields.py only because they are normalized to ISO dates, and none is featured.
